title: Coffee May Protect Your Heart — Energy Drinks Don't
paragraphs: For years, people with heart problems were often advised to avoid caffeine. However, according to a new statement from the American Heart Association (AHA), coffee may actually be linked to a lower risk of several serious health problems. At the same time, the AHA has warned that energy drinks do not appear to offer the same benefits and may even be harmful.

The scientific statement was published in the journal Circulation in July 2026. According to the statement, drinking up to five cups of coffee a day is safe for most adults. Regular coffee consumption has been linked to lower risks of stroke, type 2 diabetes and heart failure. For example, people who drank coffee regularly had a 20% to 30% lower risk of developing type 2 diabetes. In addition, among patients who had undergone a procedure to treat an irregular heartbeat, drinking coffee every day reduced the risk of the problem returning by 39%.

However, the way coffee is made appears to matter. The benefits apply only to paper-filtered coffee and instant coffee. Unfiltered coffee, such as French press, espresso and Turkish coffee, contains a substance called cafestol, which can raise levels of LDL, or "bad," cholesterol. Adding a lot of sugar and cream may also reduce the potential benefits.

In contrast, the AHA warned that highly concentrated caffeine products, such as energy drinks, energy shots and caffeine pills, do not share these benefits. In fact, energy drinks with high levels of caffeine have been linked to harm to the heart, including sudden increases in blood pressure and irregular heartbeats, even in healthy adults.

People's reactions to caffeine also vary greatly, partly because of differences in a gene that affects how quickly the liver breaks down caffeine. Some people can handle 400 milligrams of caffeine a day, which is about three to five cups of coffee, while others may experience sleep problems and higher blood pressure with much less.

According to cardiologist Jennifer Miao, people should consume caffeine in moderation, and not only for its potential health benefits. It is also important to remember that the findings on coffee are based mainly on observational studies, which show links rather than proving cause and effect. People with heart conditions should ask their doctors how much caffeine is safe for them.
